autoRoute.tip: Expose master-data models as local OpenAI / Anthropic compatible endpoints with automatic cross-protocol conversion
autoRoute.dispatchTooltip: Write into each agent as a virtual provider
autoRoute.runningHint: Starts and stops with uTools; local access only. No key validation — any key or none is accepted.
autoRoute.mappingHint: Map custom fixed model names to any master-data model; /v1/models returns only mapping names. Switch upstreams by editing mappings — agent config stays unchanged
autoRoute.selectModelsPlaceholder: Select providers and models (selecting a provider selects all)

autoRoute.mappingStatus: {ready}/{total} rows have a target (max {max}). Defaults are flash / plus / pro; names are editable and the first mapping with a duplicate name wins.
autoRoute.rewriteModelHint: Rewrite the model field in responses to the mapping name, so agents record it and their usage stats show the mapping name instead of the upstream model name. Turn off to pass the upstream model name through unchanged.
autoRoute.maxMappings: You can add at most {max} mappings
autoRoute.modelsRequired: Select the models to expose through the gateway first
autoRoute.dispatchHint: Writes the virtual provider "router" ({baseUrl}, {scope}); each dispatch replaces that provider's whole model list, and keeps it active if it already was. Mapping mode writes mapping names. Claude Code uses the Anthropic protocol, the rest use OpenAI-compatible APIs.

mcp.toggleOnHint: Enabled: written to local files. Click to disable and remove from local files

mcp.pathRequired: Enter a file path or select a file first
mcp.jsonOnly: Only .json files are supported (non-JSON files would be overwritten entirely)

mcp.targetsRemoved: ; removed this library's config from {count} unchecked location(s)
mcp.disabledToast: {name} disabled and removed from local files (kept in the cloud)
mcp.targetsDesc: All checked locations hold the same MCP config (a mirror of the enabled servers in the cloud master): toggling a switch, adding, editing, or deleting syncs to every location. Clicking "Refresh" first merges servers found in files but missing from the master, then writes everything back (the cloud master wins for duplicate names). Unchecking a location and saving removes enabled servers from that file (entries unique to other sources are kept). Many agents do not read ~/.mcp.json, so check the locations your agents actually use.
mcp.jsonHint: Only .json files are allowed. Prefer .mcp.json or mcp.json as the filename; missing directories are created automatically

dispatch.codexTooltip: Only providers using the OpenAI Chat / Responses protocol can dispatch to Codex
dispatch.minimaxTooltip: Only providers using the OpenAI Chat / Responses / Anthropic Messages protocol can dispatch to MiniMax Code; Chinese provider names are sanitized to ASCII provider keys
dispatch.qoderTooltip: Only providers using the OpenAI Chat / Responses / Anthropic Messages protocol can dispatch to Qoder; Chinese provider names are sanitized to ASCII provider keys
dispatch.zcodeTooltip: Only providers using the OpenAI Chat / Responses / Anthropic Messages protocol can dispatch to ZCode; provider names are sanitized to lowercase IDs by ZCode rules
dispatch.dshTooltip: dsh supports four protocols (manually added providers only expose OpenAI Chat / Anthropic Messages); Chinese provider names are sanitized to route names and the key is written to ~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml
dispatch.grokTooltip: Only OpenAI Chat / Responses / Anthropic Messages providers can be dispatched to Grok Build; non-ASCII provider names are sanitized into TOML keys
dispatch.clineTooltip: Only OpenAI Chat Completions providers can be dispatched to Cline; non-ASCII provider names are sanitized into provider IDs
dispatch.agentPathsHint: Claude → uTools DB config (visible on the Claude config page); OpenCode → opencode.json; Pi → models.json; omp → models.yml; Reasonix → config.toml; Codex → ~/.codex/config.toml; Kimi → ~/.kimi-code/config.toml (alias provider/modelID); MiniMax Code → ~/.minimax/config.yaml (custom_provider, keys sanitized to ASCII); Qoder → ~/.qoder/settings.json (providers, keys sanitized to ASCII); ZCode → ~/.zcode/v2/provider_config.json (custom models, IDs sanitized by ZCode rules); Hermes → ~/.hermes/config.yaml; DSH → ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml (llm-pi-ai.providers, route names sanitized to ASCII, key written to .credentials.yaml); Grok Build → ~/.grok/config.toml (model_providers + model, keys sanitized)

subscription.tip: Add the services you subscribe to; the plugin reads your browser session to fetch usage (no API key needed)

subscription.cookieFound: Session found in a local browser

subscription.loginHint: The plugin scans local browser sessions — Chromium apps (Chrome, Edge, Brave, ego lite, Quark, …), Firefox and Safari — and auto-discovers apps outside that list. On macOS the first read asks for keychain access: choose Allow. If it still fails, click "Choose folder" to point at a browser profile folder directly.
subscription.manualPlaceholder: stTb6fr9Hq4kHz… (value only is fine — the name is added for you)
subscription.manualHint: Right-click the page → Inspect → Application → Cookies → copy the value of __Secure-better-auth.session_token. Once filled, browsers are not read.
subscription.manualReloginHint: This subscription uses a pasted cookie: the edit dialog is open — paste a fresh one.
subscription.deleteConfirm: Delete this subscription? The stored session will be removed too.
subscription.expiredHint: Click "Refresh session" in the top-right: sign in in your browser first, then read again.
subscription.noSnapshot: No usage data yet. Click refresh to retry

error.unauthorized: Session expired — sign in again, then read the session
error.not_found: No session found in local browsers — sign in first
error.network: Network request failed, please retry later

subscription.keychainPrompt: An encrypted session was found but the decryption key was not available: click Allow in the macOS keychain dialog, then click "Read again".
subscription.appBoundHint: This browser uses app-bound encryption (Chrome 127+) which cannot be read. Sign in with another browser, or use "Choose folder" to point at a different profile.
subscription.unsupportedHint: This environment cannot read browser databases (Node 22.5+ required), so the session cannot be read automatically.

subscription.dirHint: Lookup order: chosen folders → built-in browser list → auto-discovery. Adding a folder skips the keychain name guessing.
